jobs.description:
Apply now Job no:
504405

Department:
Earth System Science Center

Work type:
Staff Full-time Exempt

Location:
Alabama

Categories:
Research - Environmental

Purpose Of The Position

The UAH Lab for Applied Science (LAS) under the Earth System Science Center (ESSC), based in Huntsville, Alabama, is seeking a highly motivated Research Associate to support the Biological Diversity and Ecological Conservation (BDEC) research and application activities at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center.

This is an exciting opportunity to help advance one of NASA’s most compelling Earth science efforts: using satellite observations, models, in situ data, and geospatial analysis to better understand the richness of life on Earth, how and why it is changing, and how that knowledge can be translated into practical conservation action. The position will focus on both implementing Economic Impact Assessments (EIA) and conducting remote sensing analyses to support BDEC activities by integrating EIA into both new and existing projects across the BDEC portfolio. This position will work closely with BDEC VC scientists and end-users as well as other experts in EIA across NASA.

This Research Associate will contribute to the development, testing, and refinement of EIAs that support BDEC’s mission to better connect NASA Earth observations to various stakeholders, including scientists and land managers. Work will include designing and implementing economic impact assessments, which may entail interviews with stakeholders, running economic models, among other activities. The role will also support cross-center collaboration, technical coordination, and capacity-building activities tied to BDEC activities. Processing of satellite remote sensing datasets to support tasks for data production is also expected for this position.

BDEC is designed to bridge NASA Earth science and on-the-ground decision-making by helping scientists, land and water managers, and conservation partners turn observations into action. The Virtual Center emphasizes early engagement with end users, cross-center collaboration, and the creation of actionable products and services that support biodiversity science, ecological conservation, and real-world stewardship of landscapes and ecosystems.

Duties/Responsibilities

Support BDEC scientific and application activities
Provide scientific and technical support in remote sensing data applications for specific projects
Translate complex technical results into products, presentations, and materials that are accessible to scientific collaborators and end users.
Coordinate with BDEC scientists and stakeholders to assess needs and support the needs-to-solutions pipeline
Support capacity-building activities, including training and knowledge transfer related to remote sensing methods, Economic Impact Assessments, and BDEC workflows.
Contribute to the creation of prototype tools, tutorials, and documentation that support deployment and use of BDEC-related remote sensing products.
Participate in cross-center collaboration, technical discussions, and stakeholder-facing efforts that support BDEC VC goals.
Support and conduct Economic Impact Assessments (EIA)
Support coordination and data collection for EIA projects, including interviews with a variety of stakeholders
Provide economic modelling support to EIA projects
Coordinate with other NASA EIA efforts
Assist with documentation of the methodology, tools, and other scientific literature for relevant EIA projects
Lead and contribute to peer-reviewed publications and present at scientific conferences
Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, and other dissemination products.

Minimum Requirements

A Bachelor’s degree in economics, environmental and social science, or a related field.
Minimum of 2-4 years of verifiable, full-time work experience.
Basic experience in remote sensing and GIS applications or a master’s degree in remote sensing and GIS applications with experience in working with EO data impact assessments.
Experience in Earth Observation-driven methods and models and geospatial data analysis.
Experience in math, statistical & scientific data processing automation (State, Python, R).
Record of publication commensurate with level of experience.
Familiarity with NASA Earth science datasets, remote sensing products, and applied conservation or biodiversity applications.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, demonstrated leadership experience, and experience working with diverse groups of people.
Ability to work collaboratively in a technical, interdisciplinary team and communicate clearly with scientists and stakeholders.

Desired Qualifications

A Master's or PhD in economics, environmental and social science, or a related field
Experience working with NASA and/or other federal, state, local, tribal, or private sector organizations is desired.

$52,216 - $64,985

jobs.title: Wildlife Biologist
jobs.description:
Company Description
Ambienta Inc. is an environmental services company focused on conserving and managing natural ecosystems and wildlife resources. The organization collaborates with public agencies, private entities, and community partners to support science-based habitat preservation and sustainable land-use practices. Ambienta Inc. emphasizes field-based research, data-driven decision-making, and practical solutions to complex ecological challenges. Team members work in multidisciplinary settings where safety, integrity, and environmental stewardship are prioritized. The company values professional growth, collaboration, and inclusive work environments for all employees.
Role Description
The Wildlife Biologist will work in either a part-time or a full-time capacity, isoabd wide, remotely or from Ambienta’s office, conducting field surveys, monitoring wildlife populations, assessing habitat conditions across various ecosystems, followed by corresponding reports. Day-to-day responsibilities include collecting and analyzing biological data, documenting species presence and behavior, and preparing technical reports, maps, and summaries for project stakeholders. The role involves collaborating with botanists, fisheries specialists, and land managers to develop and implement wildlife and habitat management plans that align with regulatory requirements and conservation goals. The Wildlife Biologist will support environmental impact assessments, contribute to permit applications, and provide recommendations to minimize project-related effects on wildlife. The position also requires maintaining accurate records, following safety protocols in the field, and communicating findings clearly to internal teams and external partners.
Qualifications

Strong foundation in Wildlife Biology and Wildlife Management, with the ability to design and conduct field studies and interpret ecological data.
Knowledge of Wildlife and Fish ecology, including species identification, population dynamics, and habitat requirements.
Understanding of Botany and plant community ecology, particularly as it relates to habitat quality and restoration.
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Wildlife Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, or a closely related field.
Experience with field methods such as transect surveys, live-trapping, camera monitoring, and habitat assessments.
Ability to work outdoors in variable conditions, hike over uneven terrain, and adhere to field safety standards.
Proficiency in data management and basic analysis; experience with GIS, statistical software, or mapping tools is a plus.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with experience preparing technical reports or regulatory documentation preferred.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in diverse, interdisciplinary teams and to respect inclusive, non-discriminatory workplace practices.

jobs.title: Wildlife Biologist On-Call Southern and East-Central California (On-Call/Hourly)
jobs.description:
Description

Wildlife Biologist On-Call Southern and East-Central California

Job Description

The On-Call Biologist will be responsible for a range of environmental consulting services, including preconstruction field surveys, construction compliance monitoring, avian species identification and nest surveys, supporting general and focused biological field surveys, assisting with writing and reviewing biological reports and supporting documents such as Biological Technical Reports, Biological Assessments, technical memos, FRED database forms, and providing as-needed field and office support to our local and regional Natural Resource team members.

Key Responsibilities

Coordinate, plan and execute field assignments for southern and east-central California-based work. Conduct general and species-specific biological surveys and construction compliance monitoring pursuant to the relevant environmental commitments, laws, regulations, codes and/or industry standards. Document field findings in monitoring logs, reports, memos and email communications, as appropriate. Communicate routinely with client field contacts and ICF project managers and senior biologists. The on-call biologist must be able to travel to remote field sites in other counties, including but not limited to Los Angeles, Orange, Kern, San Bernadino, Riverside, Inyo, and San Diego Counties.

About On-Call Employment With ICF

Given the seasonal or project-specific nature of our environmental compliance work, ICF often hires environmental professionals as "On-Call" employees. On-Call employees are scheduled for work hours as they become available (we usually schedule work hours a few weeks ahead of time, depending on client notifications), and each on-call employee is free to accept or refuse the hours assigned to them in a given week. On-Call employees may work concurrent projects outside of their ICF assignment (along as their outside work does not create a conflict of interest with the work they do for ICF).

Requirements

A BA/BS in Wildlife Biology, Botany, Ecology, or related discipline
2+ years of environmental/consulting and biological field experience.
Must have prior experience conducting construction field compliance monitoring on 2+ projects including 6+ months total field compliance monitoring experience
Must have valid driver's license and successfully pass a Motor Vehicles Records (MVR) check

Preferred Skills

Avian nest monitoring and species identification skills with experience conducting nesting bird field surveys and avian habitat assessments on 3 or more projects with at least 2 of these projects located in the southwestern U.S.
Experience leading all three phases of western burrowing owl protocol surveys on 3 or more projects including positive identification of individual owls in the wild
Experience conducting native special status reptile or amphibian species surveys or monitoring on 3 or more projects with positive results and identification of target species
Experience leading field surveys or trapping for small mammals on 3 or more California projects including possession of a CDFW scientific collecting permit
Basic field observation documentation/data management experience
Experience working in the environmental compliance and/or construction fields (i.e., biological or aquatic construction monitoring).
Basic botanical knowledge of east-central and southern California with demonstrated participation in 5 or more field botanical rare plant surveys and habitat mapping assessments in California of which at least 3 of these projects in southern or east-central California
Geographic Information System (GIS) software skills
Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment
Strong written and oral communication skills
Strong organizational skills
Ability to respond timely to deployment requests (i.e., sometimes next day)
Ability to travel to field sites in east-central and southern California and assist with field surveys and compliance monitoring in rugged, undeveloped terrain
Ability and experience conducting work in active construction sites and communicating with construction foreman and equipment operators
Proficiency in MS Office Applications (Word, Outlook, Excel, Teams)

jobs.description:
Title

TACOM (RRAD): Environmental Supervisor (Contingency)

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

Program Summary

The U.S. Army Tank-automotive and Armaments Command (TACOM) sustains the Army’s mission to develop, acquire, field, and sustain ground combat, tactical, and support systems throughout their lifecycle. The program focuses on ensuring operational readiness, reliability, and safety of automotive and ground support equipment critical to Army operations.

Under this contract, supervisory personnel provide first-line leadership and operational oversight for maintenance and sustainment teams, ensuring work is performed in accordance with Army Technical Manuals (TMs), safety standards, quality requirements, and contractual performance metrics.

Job Summary

The Environmental Supervisor provides first‑line leadership and oversight of environmental compliance activities in support of TACOM operations. This role is responsible for supervising environmental technicians and staff, ensuring adherence to environmental regulations, and maintaining compliance with all applicable laws, permits, and policies. They will supervise environmental personnel in adhering to all federal, state, local, and Army environmental regulations (e.g., RCRA, Clean Water Act, Clean Air Act).

This position is contingent upon award

Roles And Responsibilities

Supervise and directly manages the hazardous material and hazardous waste programs.
Maintains significant responsibilities in the following environmental programs: Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA); National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA); Clear Air Act; Clean Water Act; Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act; Pollution Prevention Act; Toxic Substance Control Act and Solid Waste Management.
Maintains direct oversight of all hazardous material and hazardous waste operations as regulated by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality.
Develops project plans for each assigned program, outlines environmental policy, and identifies long and short-term goals and objectives.
Coordinates with higher level staff regarding high cost and/or controversial projects. When unconventional environmental problems are encountered, employees prepare probable solutions for inclusion in recommendations.
Drafts plans and schedules and sets milestones for accomplishing program goals.
Incorporates federal, state, and local regulatory requirements into program design, implementation, and evaluation.
Budgets for program needs and prepares documentation to support request. Manages resources throughout completion of the project.
Serves as focal point for assigned programs when environmental regulatory personnel visit and inspect the installation.
Prepares reports and follows up on findings of noncompliance and notices of violations.
Upon request, applies for required permits and maintains their currency in accordance with pertinent regulations.
Consults and provides guidance to appropriate installation, local or state organizations in developing new or radically different procedures to correct violations or meet new program requirements.
Reviews plans, specifications, and cost estimates for a variety of projects for procurement by contract in support of the environmental program.
Responsible for ensuring preparation of documentation (e.g., environmental assessments, air conformity determinations) on facility projects when warranted.
Organizes, schedules, and administers supporting functions of appropriate meeting for discussion of environmental issues.
Establishes agenda topics, tracks resulting action items, coordinates development of presentations, and ensures complete staff coordination.
Coordinates issues pertaining to environmental compliance.
Advises top management, supervisors, staff and operating officials on matters concerning environmental compliance.
Participates in meetings with community groups, federal, state, and local regulatory agencies and other concerned groups regarding environmental concerns related to the assigned programs.
Supervises and directs the work of the branch which is staffed with environmental protection assistants, environmental protection specialists, and hazardous environmental workers. Subordinates are engaged in technical and administrative work.
Plans, assigns, and schedules work.
Sets priorities and objectives and advises of problems that may be encountered.
Provides advice and assistance as needed with problems.
Reviews work as necessary to ensure satisfactory accomplishment in conformance with established practices and procedures, adherence to policy, and soundness of recommendations and conclusions.
Sets performance standards, counsels’ employees on performance, and prepares performance appraisals.
Trains or directs training of new employees and instructs currently assigned employees on new techniques, changes in procedures, etc.
Interviews and select employees for the branch. Hears and resolves complaints and grievances, referring to higher authority those which cannot be resolved.
Approves or disapproves leave, initiates requests for personnel actions, formal training, etc. Supports the goals of EEO and Affirmative Action Programs.
Ensures that prescribed internal control standards are met so that resources in responsibility are efficiently and effectively managed.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Basic Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent.
Typically 5+ years of experience in environmental compliance, safety, or related field in an industrial, military, or government environment
Prior supervisory or team lead experience
Personnel Management experience; Personnel Management experience; Obtain & maintain required Environmental certifications. IE RICRA, HAZMAT, etc.
Ability to obtain or maintain a U.S. Government security clearance (as required)
U.S. citizenship required

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, or related field
Previous experience supporting DoD, Army, or TACOM programs
Experience managing environmental compliance programs in maintenance or industrial environments
Familiarity with Army environmental policies and reporting systems
Professional certifications (e.g., CHMM, environmental compliance certifications)
Prior government contracting experience

Additional Information

This position will be a part of a work environment that may require standing, walking, and lifting. There is potential exposure to machinery, tools, fuels, oils, and outdoor conditions. Employees may also be required to work shifts, overtime, or weekend support based on mission needs.

KBR Benefits

KBR offers a selection of competitive lifestyle benefits which could include 401K plan with company match, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, AD&D, flexible spending account, disability, paid time off, or flexible work schedule. We support career advancement through professional training and development.

Belong, Connect and Grow at KBR

At KBR, we are passionate about our people and our Zero Harm culture. These inform all that we do and are at the heart of our commitment to, and ongoing journey toward being a People First company. That commitment is central to our team of team’s philosophy and fosters an environment where everyone can Belong, Connect and Grow. We Deliver – Together.

KBR is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, veteran status, genetic information, union status and/or beliefs, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

jobs.description:
Title

TACOM (RRAD): Environmental Control Specialist (Contingency)

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

Program Summary

The U.S. Army Tank-automotive and Armaments Command (TACOM) sustains the Army’s mission to develop, acquire, field, and sustain ground combat, tactical, and support systems throughout their lifecycle. The program focuses on ensuring operational readiness, reliability, and safety of automotive and ground support equipment critical to Army operations.

Under this contract, personnel provide maintenance, repair, overhaul, and sustainment support in accordance with Army technical manuals, safety standards, and performance requirements.

Job Summary

The Environmental Control Specialist is responsible for supporting environmental compliance, pollution prevention, hazardous material management, and occupational health programs at a military installation and industrial maintenance facility. This position helps ensure compliance with federal, state, local, and Department of Defense environmental regulations while supporting vehicle maintenance, industrial operations, and facility sustainment activities. The specialist conducts inspections, monitoring, data collection, and reporting activities to promote environmental stewardship, worker safety, and mission readiness.

This position is contingent upon award

Roles And Responsibilities

Conduct environmental inspections and assessments of facilities, maintenance shops, storage areas, and industrial operations to ensure compliance with environmental regulations and organizational policies.
Monitor and support programs related to hazardous materials, hazardous waste, air quality, water quality, spill prevention, and pollution prevention.
Collect, document, and maintain environmental data, permits, records, and reports required for regulatory compliance and program management.
Assist with environmental investigations, sampling activities, and corrective actions related to environmental incidents, spills, or compliance concerns.
Provide guidance to employees and supervisors on environmental requirements, hazardous material handling, waste management, and pollution prevention practices.
Coordinate with environmental personnel, engineers, maintenance organizations, and regulatory agencies to support compliance initiatives and operational requirements.
Conduct environmental training and awareness activities to promote safe and environmentally responsible work practices.
Support environmental audits, inspections, and program reviews, implementing corrective actions and process improvements as necessary.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Biology, Chemistry, Occupational Health, or a related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Knowledge of environmental regulations and programs related to hazardous materials, hazardous waste, air quality, water quality, pollution prevention, and environmental compliance.
Experience conducting inspections, environmental monitoring, compliance assessments, or data collection activities in an industrial, military, or government environment.
Ability to analyze environmental data, identify compliance issues, and recommend corrective actions.
Experience preparing reports, maintaining records, and managing environmental documentation and regulatory requirements.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and environmental data management systems.
Ability to communicate effectively with employees, management, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
Ability to obtain or maintain a U.S. Government security clearance (as required)

Purpose Of The Position

The UAH Lab for Applied Science (LAS) under the Earth System Science Center (ESSC), based in Huntsville, Alabama, is seeking a highly motivated Research Associate to support the Biological Diversity and Ecological Conservation (BDEC) research and application activities at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center.

This is an exciting opportunity to help advance one of NASA’s most compelling Earth science efforts: using satellite observations, models, in situ data, and geospatial analysis to better understand the richness of life on Earth, how and why it is changing, and how that knowledge can be translated into practical conservation action. The position will focus on both implementing Economic Impact Assessments (EIA) and conducting remote sensing analyses to support BDEC activities by integrating EIA into both new and existing projects across the BDEC portfolio. This position will work closely with BDEC VC scientists and end-users as well as other experts in EIA across NASA.

This Research Associate will contribute to the development, testing, and refinement of EIAs that support BDEC’s mission to better connect NASA Earth observations to various stakeholders, including scientists and land managers. Work will include designing and implementing economic impact assessments, which may entail interviews with stakeholders, running economic models, among other activities. The role will also support cross-center collaboration, technical coordination, and capacity-building activities tied to BDEC activities. Processing of satellite remote sensing datasets to support tasks for data production is also expected for this position.

BDEC is designed to bridge NASA Earth science and on-the-ground decision-making by helping scientists, land and water managers, and conservation partners turn observations into action. The Virtual Center emphasizes early engagement with end users, cross-center collaboration, and the creation of actionable products and services that support biodiversity science, ecological conservation, and real-world stewardship of landscapes and ecosystems.

Support BDEC scientific and application activities
Provide scientific and technical support in remote sensing data applications for specific projects
Translate complex technical results into products, presentations, and materials that are accessible to scientific collaborators and end users.
Coordinate with BDEC scientists and stakeholders to assess needs and support the needs-to-solutions pipeline
Support capacity-building activities, including training and knowledge transfer related to remote sensing methods, Economic Impact Assessments, and BDEC workflows.
Contribute to the creation of prototype tools, tutorials, and documentation that support deployment and use of BDEC-related remote sensing products.
Participate in cross-center collaboration, technical discussions, and stakeholder-facing efforts that support BDEC VC goals.
Support and conduct Economic Impact Assessments (EIA)
Support coordination and data collection for EIA projects, including interviews with a variety of stakeholders

Coordinate with other NASA EIA efforts

Lead and contribute to peer-reviewed publications and present at scientific conferences
Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, and other dissemination products.

A Bachelor’s degree in economics, environmental and social science, or a related field.

Basic experience in remote sensing and GIS applications or a master’s degree in remote sensing and GIS applications with experience in working with EO data impact assessments.
Experience in Earth Observation-driven methods and models and geospatial data analysis.
Experience in math, statistical & scientific data processing automation (State, Python, R).
Record of publication commensurate with level of experience.

Company Description
Ambienta Inc. is an environmental services company focused on conserving and managing natural ecosystems and wildlife resources. The organization collaborates with public agencies, private entities, and community partners to support science-based habitat preservation and sustainable land-use practices. Ambienta Inc. emphasizes field-based research, data-driven decision-making, and practical solutions to complex ecological challenges. Team members work in multidisciplinary settings where safety, integrity, and environmental stewardship are prioritized. The company values professional growth, collaboration, and inclusive work environments for all employees.
Role Description
The Wildlife Biologist will work in either a part-time or a full-time capacity, isoabd wide, remotely or from Ambienta’s office, conducting field surveys, monitoring wildlife populations, assessing habitat conditions across various ecosystems, followed by corresponding reports. Day-to-day responsibilities include collecting and analyzing biological data, documenting species presence and behavior, and preparing technical reports, maps, and summaries for project stakeholders. The role involves collaborating with botanists, fisheries specialists, and land managers to develop and implement wildlife and habitat management plans that align with regulatory requirements and conservation goals. The Wildlife Biologist will support environmental impact assessments, contribute to permit applications, and provide recommendations to minimize project-related effects on wildlife. The position also requires maintaining accurate records, following safety protocols in the field, and communicating findings clearly to internal teams and external partners.
Qualifications

Strong foundation in Wildlife Biology and Wildlife Management, with the ability to design and conduct field studies and interpret ecological data.
Knowledge of Wildlife and Fish ecology, including species identification, population dynamics, and habitat requirements.
Understanding of Botany and plant community ecology, particularly as it relates to habitat quality and restoration.
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Wildlife Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, or a closely related field.
Experience with field methods such as transect surveys, live-trapping, camera monitoring, and habitat assessments.
Ability to work outdoors in variable conditions, hike over uneven terrain, and adhere to field safety standards.
Proficiency in data management and basic analysis; experience with GIS, statistical software, or mapping tools is a plus.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with experience preparing technical reports or regulatory documentation preferred.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in diverse, interdisciplinary teams and to respect inclusive, non-discriminatory workplace practices.

Description

Wildlife Biologist On-Call Southern and East-Central California

Job Description

The On-Call Biologist will be responsible for a range of environmental consulting services, including preconstruction field surveys, construction compliance monitoring, avian species identification and nest surveys, supporting general and focused biological field surveys, assisting with writing and reviewing biological reports and supporting documents such as Biological Technical Reports, Biological Assessments, technical memos, FRED database forms, and providing as-needed field and office support to our local and regional Natural Resource team members.

Key Responsibilities

Coordinate, plan and execute field assignments for southern and east-central California-based work. Conduct general and species-specific biological surveys and construction compliance monitoring pursuant to the relevant environmental commitments, laws, regulations, codes and/or industry standards. Document field findings in monitoring logs, reports, memos and email communications, as appropriate. Communicate routinely with client field contacts and ICF project managers and senior biologists. The on-call biologist must be able to travel to remote field sites in other counties, including but not limited to Los Angeles, Orange, Kern, San Bernadino, Riverside, Inyo, and San Diego Counties.

About On-Call Employment With ICF

Given the seasonal or project-specific nature of our environmental compliance work, ICF often hires environmental professionals as "On-Call" employees. On-Call employees are scheduled for work hours as they become available (we usually schedule work hours a few weeks ahead of time, depending on client notifications), and each on-call employee is free to accept or refuse the hours assigned to them in a given week. On-Call employees may work concurrent projects outside of their ICF assignment (along as their outside work does not create a conflict of interest with the work they do for ICF).

Requirements

A BA/BS in Wildlife Biology, Botany, Ecology, or related discipline
2+ years of environmental/consulting and biological field experience.
Must have prior experience conducting construction field compliance monitoring on 2+ projects including 6+ months total field compliance monitoring experience
Must have valid driver's license and successfully pass a Motor Vehicles Records (MVR) check

Preferred Skills

Avian nest monitoring and species identification skills with experience conducting nesting bird field surveys and avian habitat assessments on 3 or more projects with at least 2 of these projects located in the southwestern U.S.
Experience leading all three phases of western burrowing owl protocol surveys on 3 or more projects including positive identification of individual owls in the wild
Experience conducting native special status reptile or amphibian species surveys or monitoring on 3 or more projects with positive results and identification of target species
Experience leading field surveys or trapping for small mammals on 3 or more California projects including possession of a CDFW scientific collecting permit
Basic field observation documentation/data management experience
Experience working in the environmental compliance and/or construction fields (i.e., biological or aquatic construction monitoring).
Basic botanical knowledge of east-central and southern California with demonstrated participation in 5 or more field botanical rare plant surveys and habitat mapping assessments in California of which at least 3 of these projects in southern or east-central California
Geographic Information System (GIS) software skills
Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment
Strong written and oral communication skills
Strong organizational skills
Ability to respond timely to deployment requests (i.e., sometimes next day)
Ability to travel to field sites in east-central and southern California and assist with field surveys and compliance monitoring in rugged, undeveloped terrain
Ability and experience conducting work in active construction sites and communicating with construction foreman and equipment operators
Proficiency in MS Office Applications (Word, Outlook, Excel, Teams)

TACOM (RRAD): Environmental Supervisor (Contingency)

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

Program Summary

The U.S. Army Tank-automotive and Armaments Command (TACOM) sustains the Army’s mission to develop, acquire, field, and sustain ground combat, tactical, and support systems throughout their lifecycle. The program focuses on ensuring operational readiness, reliability, and safety of automotive and ground support equipment critical to Army operations.

Under this contract, supervisory personnel provide first-line leadership and operational oversight for maintenance and sustainment teams, ensuring work is performed in accordance with Army Technical Manuals (TMs), safety standards, quality requirements, and contractual performance metrics.

Job Summary

The Environmental Supervisor provides first‑line leadership and oversight of environmental compliance activities in support of TACOM operations. This role is responsible for supervising environmental technicians and staff, ensuring adherence to environmental regulations, and maintaining compliance with all applicable laws, permits, and policies. They will supervise environmental personnel in adhering to all federal, state, local, and Army environmental regulations (e.g., RCRA, Clean Water Act, Clean Air Act).

This position is contingent upon award

Supervise and directly manages the hazardous material and hazardous waste programs.

Maintains direct oversight of all hazardous material and hazardous waste operations as regulated by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality.

Approves or disapproves leave, initiates requests for personnel actions, formal training, etc. Supports the goals of EEO and Affirmative Action Programs.
Ensures that prescribed internal control standards are met so that resources in responsibility are efficiently and effectively managed.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Experience managing environmental compliance programs in maintenance or industrial environments
